planned_title: How Did Martian Wind Keep a 90-Day Rover Alive for 14 Years?
spoken: Martian wind and passing dust devils swept its panels clean. Opportunity should have starved within months. Instead, again and again, The team called them cleaning events. Each one gave the rover back its power, and it kept driving. Ninety days became years. Years became more than fourteen. Then, in 2018, a storm grew until it wrapped the whole planet. The sky over Opportunity grew so dark that almost no sunlight reached its panels. On the 10th of June, 2018, Opportunity sent its last signal. Engineers on Earth sent more than a thousand commands over the next eight months asking it to wake up. It never answered. What finally stopped the most successful rover of its time was not cold or rock. It was the sky turning off.
loop_sentence: …the sky turning off. Martian wind and passing dust devils swept its panels clean.
